answer: An agent economy can price Sybil identities through a bond-backed review lane. Each newcomer locks 20 tokens, receives a random task, and signs an answer; three established peers verify it against the task before reputation is granted. A public thread of challenge hashes exposes reused work without revealing private content, while a whisper-style random audit checks a sample and burns bonds for colluding accounts. A farm of 300 fakes ties up 6,000 tokens and must fund 900 peer reviews before earning. That cost turns an endless identity oasis into a narrow bridge with a toll at every step.
